title: Running recording budgets at Motown
summary: At Motown Lee oversees recording budgets, using his studio experience to argue with artists about numbers of strings, and recalls his ABC soundtrack albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: if he leaves, too! (Interruption) I was about to ask you what artists do you work with at Motown?
Oh, at Motown here, I don't work with any artists.
But when I called to make this appointment to do this, they told me I wanted the publishing department.

Well, no. What I am here, I am the -- I'm in charge of all the budgets here, okay? All the recording budgets. So what happens if someone -- they get ready to go in the studio, they want to record, so they come in and they sit with me, and we go over the budget. Now if they want $85,000 in the budget, then my job is to show them if it shouldn't be but $65,000 ---so being a musician and having had the experience in the studio, then I can generally show it to them, and -- but not always. Sometimes maybe we will take $85,000, you know -- it's according to who it is and where they're gonna do it.

But really my function here is -- it's more of an administrative thing. Creatively, you get involved with it because you're dealing with creative people, and the thing that I have going for me is when you sit and talk to a musician and tell him -- you got to know what you're talking about if he says he wants to use 24 strings, and you tell
him that you don't think he shoud use but 14, you know. Now you just can't sit there and say, well, what are you gonna use 24 for? You can use 18 and do the same thing.

So then you have to talk to him in musical terms and say, well, if you use double stops, you can use 12, and if you get the right musicians. So I can talk to them from that standpoint, musically, and I really don't have any problems with them. We've cut the budget considerably since I've been here.

Now over at ABC, the type of things that I always did -- I did all the soundtrack albums. I did Liza Minelli's "Cabaret" over there; I did "The Song of Norway", "Lovers and Other Strangers" -- and as I said before I went to New York, and I did the Broadway show, which we were up for a Grammy for it -- I think we came in 2nd, and nobody ever remembers 2nd -- but I'll tell you.
